blocks.text: 握手协商与名字准入是两个独立阶段，默认各为 10,000 ms。timeout-only 的 `connect: { timeoutMs }` 也可设置其他来源的名字准入期限；等待中的对端按 `pending` 通知里的剩余时间等待，重复通知不会刷新期限。最坏等待接近两阶段之和。短配置支持 `entry`、`command/args`、`cwd`、显式环境、`wrap`、原生限制与 `supervision`。限制的实际效果取决于运行环境，配置不会创造原生隔离能力。
推荐每个 Host 只安装一种传输；同一传输可有多个会话。若确需混装不同传输，使用互不冲突的 namespace 并明确路由和权限，不把它们当成同质成员池。
根入口运行时导出 `processPlugin`、`isProcessChild`、`RpcProcessErrorCode` 与 `RPC_PROCESS_ERROR_SOURCE`；同时导出选项和原生来源类型。`name` 是本地注册名，`namespace` 决定调用入口，`expose` 是普通 PluginHost 的显式本地 Feature 白名单。

调用使用 `host.process.request/notify/stream/group` 和定向的 `host.process.send`。根对象保留 `self`、`provide`、`close`，不提供这些调用方法。原生成员查询、控制与事件位于 `host.process.members`，例如 `list/get/stop/kill/restart/replace/on/watch`；借用连接不因此取得终止外部进程的权限。

`/features` 导出完整实例工厂 `sendQueueFeature`、`flowControlFeature`、`ipcLogFeature`；实例放进 `processPlugin({ features })`。`sendQueueFeature({ flow })` 可借用同一个 flow 实例，不能另配一套容量。业务 timeout/retry 也通过传输的 `features` 选择。host 介入插件使用 `@migaia/rpc-host/plugins/*`，在传输之前安装。

使用唯一的 `migaia.rpc/2` 协议。`@migaia/rpc-contract/protocol` 提供纯协议数据与准入；`/interfaces` 提供能力类型，`/errors` 与 `/error-code` 提供错误契约。Contract 不执行 I/O、业务 schema 或监督。业务校验由 `/plugins/schema` 负责；自定义载体作者使用 `@migaia/rpc-host/sdk`，复用 canonical carrier，而不是返回另一个 Host 或端点。

原生 token/bootstrap 存在不等于已完成自动 verifier、principal 或跨重连认证 scope；这些边界尚有未闭合项。不要据此推断身份可信或业务可安全重放。Host 关闭与已接纳业务 drain 的顺序、重启 downtime 的无目标错误、同名准入错误呈现仍有保留的行为差异。IPC 容量拒绝保留 `OVERLOADED`；实际物理 I/O 失败仍按 `TRANSPORT` 保留原 cause，准入失败不表示已经写出。
启动通道在实际关闭阶段可直接报告 `PROCESS_CHANNEL_CLOSED`；真实 `EPIPE` 等原生错误仍在错误图可达，不要求重复嵌套两个同码包装。业务 `timeout: false` 关闭选中的业务期限，不自动添加 Process 调用硬上限。
按 `source/code/cause` 处理错误并保留原生原因。完整迁移验收尚未完成；上述差异不作为已实现保证。详细配置见使用指南。

一个 Host 通常选择一种传输。根对象管理 `self/provide/close`，业务调用在 namespace 下；Process 的默认 namespace 为 `process`。下面所有 TypeScript 模块按当前公开 dist 做类型检查，不代表真实环境和认证验收已完成。
同一个连接两端都可提供业务。下面是 Node/POSIX 本机命名服务的调用形态；它不证明该服务已配置认证。
`request` 没有目标时使用当前 namespace 的直连集合，多个目标保留各自结果；`send(nameOrId, method, payload)` 只选择一个当前直连。业务流保留自己的迭代器与取消，不代表拥有整个原生进程。重启期间的零会话请求与旧 downtime 错误之间仍有未闭合差异，应用不能把空集合当作重启完成。

blocks.text: 原生容量、FIFO 与日志属于 Process。下例只安装一个 flow，再让 queue 和 log 借用它；timeout 是该传输选择的业务 feature，probe 是启动前的 host 介入插件。
调用者负责最终 `await host.close()`。也可单装 `flowControlFeature`，或让 `sendQueueFeature` 自建默认 flow；显式 `flow` 和重复的容量字段会在冷配置拒绝。不要把这些实例当作 host 根配置开关，也不要再提供已删除的 `ipc.log` fallback 字段。仅装 `ipcLogFeature` 不会自动启用限流。
`/features/send-queue`、`/features/flow-control`、`/features/log` 也提供对应工厂。排队取消和容量计数使用真实安装；与 batch 合用时的每逻辑调用计费仍未完成验收。容量拒绝保留 `OVERLOADED`，真实物理 I/O 失败使用 `TRANSPORT` 并保留原 cause。

`connect: { target, timeoutMs? }` 选择已有服务；timeout-only 的 `connect` 可修饰 spawn/listen/parent。协商阶段默认 10,000 ms；随后名字准入用 `connect.timeoutMs`，默认也为 10,000 ms，`pending` 传递尚未用完的协商时间与本次名字探测预算之和；只在首次通知延长期限，重复通知不会刷新。`connectTimeoutMs` 则是命名本机来源的查找等待。单次业务调用使用完整 `timeoutFeature(...)` feature 或 `timeout: false`，并可传 `signal`；这些期限相互独立。
`spawn` 可选主入口、路径/URL、短启动配置或完整原生 recipe。主入口自派生写法见 README。原生 `supervision` 保留重启、健康检查和停止策略；恢复连接不重放未确认业务。stdio 的 stdout 属于 RPC，应用日志使用 stderr。

自动 verifier/principal、跨重连 session/scope 与部分 native auth 接线尚有缺口。不要用 token、环境值、自报身份或客户端 ID 代替实际准入。需要业务认证、schema、分片、合批或类型生成时，选择实际的 `/plugins/auth`、`/plugins/schema`、`/plugins/chunk`、`/plugins/batch`、`/plugins/typegen`；它们不是 Contract 内部或传输配置字段。flow 插件必须在传输开始前安装，启动后追加会拒绝。
查询和控制使用 `host.process.members`；`list/get` 返回原生来源的安全描述，`on/watch` 观察真实事件。`stop/kill/restart/replace` 取决于实际成员归属；接入外部服务不会获得远程进程控制权。
同一冷定义可安装在原生 PluginHost 上，不另开第二个 Host。普通安装的 `expose` 必须指向真实已安装 Feature，并显式列白名单；业务仍通过 process namespace 调用。自定义载体使用 `@migaia/rpc-host/sdk`，不使用已删除的部署 assembler 或返回端点的 source。
拥有的子进程由真实监督器停止；借用服务仅释放本端连接。关闭监听器不授予终止客户端进程的权限。`close()` 是清理请求，不应推断所有已接纳业务都能 drain 完成；Host 关闭顺序与原 drain 业务仍有真实未闭合项。
通道启动失败按真实阶段保留 `PROCESS_CHANNEL_CLOSED`、连接失败或原生 `EPIPE`，不保证固定两层同码错误壳。应沿 `cause/errors` 读取原生错误，不按固定深度取值。`timeout: false` 不添加 Process 业务调用期限；原生启动、health 与 stop 预算仍各归自己的 owner。
当前同名准入的公开错误呈现也有保留的失败用例；不能把通用启动包装错误当作已完成原错误契约。为应用使用唯一身份，不用注册名推断远端 identity。按 `source/code/cause/errors` 保留错误链和原生类型；不要把未知结果当作从未执行，也不要从连接恢复推出幂等重放或持久 outcome 已建立。
`@migaia/rpc-contract` 只负责纯数据、类型、错误与协议准入；业务 schema 和策略归实际 plugin/feature，原生资源归 Process，调用生命周期归 Host。完整迁移验收尚未闭合。

blocks.text: Handshake negotiation and name admission have separate deadlines, each defaulting to 10,000 ms. A timeout-only `connect: { timeoutMs }` also sets name admission for the other sources. A waiting peer follows the remaining budget in `pending`; repeated notices never refresh it. Worst-case waiting approaches the sum of both phases. Short options include `entry`, `command/args`, `cwd`, explicit environment, `wrap`, native limits and `supervision`. Actual limits depend on the runtime; configuration does not grant native isolation.

Prefer one transport kind per Host; it may have many sessions. If different transports must share a Host, use distinct namespaces and explicit routing and permissions. They are not a homogeneous member pool.

Runtime root exports are `processPlugin`, `isProcessChild`, `RpcProcessErrorCode` and `RPC_PROCESS_ERROR_SOURCE`, alongside option/native-source types. `name` is local registration identity, `namespace` selects the call surface, and `expose` is an ordinary PluginHost's explicit local Feature allowlist.

Use `host.process.request/notify/stream/group` and targeted `host.process.send`. The root retains `self`, `provide` and `close`, without those call methods. Native member queries, controls and events live under `host.process.members`: `list/get/stop/kill/restart/replace/on/watch`. Borrowing a connection does not authorize terminating its external process.

`/features` exports complete-instance factories `sendQueueFeature`, `flowControlFeature` and `ipcLogFeature`; pass instances to `processPlugin({ features })`. `sendQueueFeature({ flow })` can borrow that same flow instance without another capacity policy. Business timeout/retry are also selected through transport `features`. Host intervention plugins use `@migaia/rpc-host/plugins/*` and install before transports.

The sole profile is `migaia.rpc/2`. `@migaia/rpc-contract/protocol` provides pure protocol data and admission; `/interfaces` provides capability types, and `/errors` plus `/error-code` provide error contracts. Contract performs no I/O, business schema validation or supervision. `/plugins/schema` owns business validation. Custom carrier authors use `@migaia/rpc-host/sdk` and canonical carriers rather than returning another Host or endpoint.

A native token/bootstrap does not establish completed automatic verification, principal identity or authenticated scope across reconnects; these boundaries have unresolved items. Do not infer trusted identity or safe business replay. Host close versus accepted-work drain, untargeted errors during restart downtime and same-name admission diagnostics retain known behavioral differences. IPC capacity rejection retains `OVERLOADED`; actual physical I/O failure retains `TRANSPORT` with its original cause. Admission failure does not mean a write happened.

A startup channel may directly report `PROCESS_CHANNEL_CLOSED` at the actual close phase. Native failures such as `EPIPE` remain reachable without requiring two nested wrappers carrying the same code. Business `timeout: false` disables the selected business deadline and adds no Process call cap.
Inspect `source/code/cause` and retain native causes. Full migration acceptance remains pending; these differences are not implementation guarantees. See the usage guide.
README · 中文

A Host normally selects one transport kind. The root owns `self/provide/close`; calls live under a namespace, `process` by default. These complete TypeScript modules are checked against current public dist, not proof of native-environment or authentication acceptance.
Both sides of a connection may provide methods. This Node/POSIX named-service example demonstrates calls without asserting completed service authentication.

Untargeted `request` uses the current namespace's direct targets, retaining per-target results for several peers. `send(nameOrId, method, payload)` selects one current direct peer. A business stream owns its iterator/cancellation, not the entire native process. Empty-session calls during restart still differ from the old downtime error; an empty set does not indicate completed recovery.

Native capacities, FIFO and logging belong to Process. This installs one flow and lends it to queue/log. Timeout is a transport-selected business feature; probe is a host intervention plugin installed before transport startup.

The caller eventually awaits `host.close()`. A standalone `flowControlFeature` is supported, and `sendQueueFeature` may own a default flow. Supplying an explicit flow alongside duplicate capacity fields fails during cold configuration. These are not host-root configuration switches; the old `ipc.log` fallback field is removed. Logging alone does not enable throttling.

`/features/send-queue`, `/features/flow-control` and `/features/log` expose their corresponding factories. Cancellation and capacity use actual installed owners. Per-logical-call accounting with batch remains unverified. Capacity rejection retains `OVERLOADED`; actual physical I/O failure uses `TRANSPORT` with its original cause.

`connect: { target, timeoutMs? }` selects an existing service; timeout-only connect also decorates spawn/listen/parent. Negotiation defaults to 10,000 ms; name admission then uses `connect.timeoutMs`, also 10,000 ms by default. `pending` carries the unspent negotiation time plus this one name-probe budget; only the first notice extends the deadline, and repeated notices never refresh it. `connectTimeoutMs` bounds named-local discovery. Business calls use a complete `timeoutFeature(...)` feature or `timeout: false`, with an optional `signal`; these deadlines remain independent.

Spawn accepts the main entry, a path/URL, short options or a complete native recipe. See README for self-spawn. Native `supervision` retains restart, health and stop policy; reconnection does not replay unconfirmed work. stdout belongs to stdio RPC; application logs use stderr.

Automatic verification/principal, session/scope across reconnects and parts of native auth wiring remain incomplete. A token, environment value, claimed identity or client ID is not admission proof. Select actual `/plugins/auth`, `/plugins/schema`, `/plugins/chunk`, `/plugins/batch` and `/plugins/typegen` when needed. These are neither Contract internals nor transport configuration fields. Flow plugins install before transport startup; adding them afterward rejects.

Use `host.process.members` for queries and controls. `list/get` return safe native-source descriptions; `on/watch` observe actual events. `stop/kill/restart/replace` depend on genuine ownership. Connecting to an external service does not grant remote process control.

The same cold definition installs on the actual PluginHost without creating another Host. Ordinary `expose` names real installed Features through an explicit allowlist; calls still use the process namespace. Custom carriers use `@migaia/rpc-host/sdk`, without a retired assembler or endpoint-returning source.

Real supervisors stop owned children; borrowed services release only the local connection. Closing a listener grants no authority to terminate client processes. `close()` requests cleanup; do not assume every accepted operation drains successfully. Host close order versus original drain behavior remains unresolved.

Startup failures retain the actual channel-close, connection-failure or native `EPIPE` phase without promising two identical coded shells. Follow `cause/errors` rather than a fixed depth. `timeout: false` adds no Process business-call deadline; native startup, health and stop budgets remain separate.

Same-name admission diagnostics retain a failing oracle; a generic startup wrapper does not satisfy the original error contract. Use unique application identities rather than deriving remote identity from a registration name. Retain `source/code/cause/errors`, native types and stacks. An unknown result does not prove non-execution; recovery does not establish idempotent replay or persistent outcomes.

`@migaia/rpc-contract` owns pure data, types, errors and protocol admission. Actual plugins/features own business schema and policy, Process owns native resources, and Host owns call lifetime. Full migration acceptance remains pending.

symbols.purpose: Table of the stable error codes of this package; values are the strings on `error.code`.
symbols.core:
usageSampleFailed: `PROCESS_USAGE_SAMPLE_FAILED`: CPU or memory sampling failed; show unavailable.
hostInvalidOption: `PROCESS_HOST_INVALID_OPTION`: a host option is invalid; fix the named field.
hostClosed: `PROCESS_HOST_CLOSED`: the outlet is releasing; use a new host or Peer.
handshakeTimeout: `PROCESS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT`: the handshake did not finish in time; open a new channel.
authRejected: `PROCESS_CHANNEL_AUTH_REJECTED`: the credential was refused; do not retry with it.
channelClosed: `PROCESS_CHANNEL_CLOSED`: work on a closed channel; reconnect and reconcile.
connectFailed: `PROCESS_CHANNEL_CONNECT_FAILED`: connecting to the other process, starting it, or setting up part of the channel failed. If the system call that starts the process or opens its streams throws, you get that same error object with its type, stack and fields intact. Its `source` becomes this package and its system `code` (such as `ENOENT`) becomes `PROCESS_CHANNEL_CONNECT_FAILED`, one stable value to check. An already wrapped failure keeps the original on `cause`.
listenFailed: `PROCESS_CHANNEL_LISTEN_FAILED`: preparing to listen, or binding the listening address, failed. You receive the same system error object, with its type, stack and other fields unchanged; it only gains this package as `source` and `PROCESS_CHANNEL_LISTEN_FAILED` as `code`. Both the reported error and the rejected promise keep the original `cause` chain.
pluginInvalidOption: `PROCESS_PLUGIN_INVALID_OPTION`: a plugin or source option is invalid.
resilienceInvalidOption: `PROCESS_RESILIENCE_INVALID_OPTION`: a governance limit is invalid.
connectionLimit: `PROCESS_CONNECTION_LIMIT`: connection, rate or payload limit; the call did not run.
instanceUnhealthy: `PROCESS_INSTANCE_UNHEALTHY`: the target is suspended until a healthy replacement is ready.
healthPingFailed: `PROCESS_HEALTH_PING_FAILED`: a health ping failed; supervision restarts it.
terminalCall: `PROCESS_TERMINAL_CALL`: the registration is terminal and refuses calls.
liquidated: `PROCESS_LIQUIDATED`: the registration was liquidated; create a new one.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
usageSampleFailed: `PROCESS_USAGE_SAMPLE_FAILED`: CPU or memory sampling failed; show unavailable.
hostInvalidOption: `PROCESS_HOST_INVALID_OPTION`: a host option is invalid; fix the named field.
hostClosed: `PROCESS_HOST_CLOSED`: the outlet is releasing; use a new host or Peer.
handshakeTimeout: `PROCESS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT`: the handshake did not finish in time; open a new channel.
authRejected: `PROCESS_CHANNEL_AUTH_REJECTED`: the credential was refused; do not retry with it.
channelClosed: `PROCESS_CHANNEL_CLOSED`: work on a closed channel; reconnect and reconcile.
connectFailed: `PROCESS_CHANNEL_CONNECT_FAILED`: connecting to the other process, starting it, or setting up part of the channel failed. If the system call that starts the process or opens its streams throws, you get that same error object with its type, stack and fields intact. Its `source` becomes this package and its system `code` (such as `ENOENT`) becomes `PROCESS_CHANNEL_CONNECT_FAILED`, one stable value to check. An already wrapped failure keeps the original on `cause`.
listenFailed: `PROCESS_CHANNEL_LISTEN_FAILED`: preparing to listen, or binding the listening address, failed. You receive the same system error object, with its type, stack and other fields unchanged; it only gains this package as `source` and `PROCESS_CHANNEL_LISTEN_FAILED` as `code`. Both the reported error and the rejected promise keep the original `cause` chain.
pluginInvalidOption: `PROCESS_PLUGIN_INVALID_OPTION`: a plugin or source option is invalid.
resilienceInvalidOption: `PROCESS_RESILIENCE_INVALID_OPTION`: a governance limit is invalid.
connectionLimit: `PROCESS_CONNECTION_LIMIT`: connection, rate or payload limit; the call did not run.
instanceUnhealthy: `PROCESS_INSTANCE_UNHEALTHY`: the target is suspended until a healthy replacement is ready.
healthPingFailed: `PROCESS_HEALTH_PING_FAILED`: a health ping failed; supervision restarts it.
terminalCall: `PROCESS_TERMINAL_CALL`: the registration is terminal and refuses calls.
liquidated: `PROCESS_LIQUIDATED`: the registration was liquidated; create a new one.
